name: network_layout
notes: Hand-crafted expert Procedural Graph (paper Mode 1) for the network-layout procedure, transcribed 2026-09-16 from .claude/rules/network-layout.md's Placement Procedure and Anti-Patterns sections. `guidance` values are verbatim quotes (at most two sentences) of the matching Placement Procedure step or formula; `pitfalls` values are verbatim Anti-Patterns bullets, or "" where none applies; `condition` is one clause. Producer-side contract only -- see tools/pg_actions.py's PG_RELATIONS / PG_EDGE_FIELDS and docs/adr/0011-procedural-graph-state-lives-outside-the-tox.md for the claude-context-local consumer this mirrors without talking to it.

edges.condition: all positions batched in advance
edges.guidance: Batch-compute all positions before placing anything. Never place one operator, then figure out where the next one goes.

edges.condition: dock slots computed from the host's size and dock count
edges.guidance: Row Y: row_y = sy - dh - 30 -- a tight ~30-unit gap directly below the host's bottom edge. Do NOT drop a full grid step (200) below; that produces the "stranded op with a long diagonal wire" look, not a docked companion hugging its host.
edges.pitfalls: Leaving docked callback/info DATs at their auto-spawn position. TD drops them at arbitrary coordinates whenever they're created, whether by hand or by script.

edges.condition: all positions batched in advance
edges.guidance: Batch-compute all positions before placing anything. Never place one operator, then figure out where the next one goes.
edges.pitfalls: Using fixed offsets like nodeX + 300 without accounting for nodeWidth -- this is the #1 cause of overlapping operators when ops are wider than ~100 units.

edges.condition: wiring done
edges.guidance: Place, connect, then update the annotation to enclose the new operators, expanding its width/height as needed.
edges.pitfalls: Creating operators without updating the enclosing annotation.

edges.condition: op exists and sits at (0, 0)
edges.guidance: Place, connect, then update the annotation to enclose the new operators, expanding its width/height as needed.
edges.pitfalls: Leaving script-created ops at (0, 0) / overlapping -- the most common layout failure; TD's bare .create() always drops new ops there. Position + Verify every time, regardless of how the ops were created.

edges.condition: op type auto-spawns docked companions
edges.guidance: Some operators auto-spawn companion ops docked to them (anything in op.docked) -- callback DATs, info DATs, shader DATs, keys.
edges.pitfalls: Leaving docked callback/info DATs at their auto-spawn position. TD drops them at arbitrary coordinates whenever they're created, whether by hand or by script.

edges.condition: target group chosen, or a new group decided
edges.guidance: Compute position: use each operator's actual nodeWidth/nodeHeight. New operators extend the group to the right: rightmost_nodeX + rightmost_nodeWidth + 200 (snapped to 200-unit grid).
edges.pitfalls: Placing "near" a related op by picking a mathematically close but visually wrong position -- filling a gap in the middle of a finished row instead of extending rightward.

edges.condition: group chosen and only its annotation needs changing
edges.guidance: Expand annotations when adding operators. Recalculate the bounding box with padding after every addition.
edges.pitfalls: Creating operators without updating the enclosing annotation.

edges.condition: docked list is non-empty and the slots are not yet computed
edges.guidance: Layout formula -- given host op bottom-left (sx,sy), size (sw,sh), and N docks (use the max dw,dh across docks for uniform spacing). Docked ops HUG the host -- they are the one deliberate exception to 200-grid spacing; place them tight, never a full grid step away.

edges.condition: docked list is non-empty
edges.guidance: Procedure (for scripted builds): after creating any op in a script, query op.docked, reposition every docked op per the layout formula (set nodeX/nodeY directly), then re-check the layout to confirm the docked row landed directly under the host with no overlap.

edges.condition: layout read and it is not already messy; if every op sits at the origin, treat all of them as new
edges.guidance: Identify the target group: determine which annotation group the new operator belongs to. If none fits, you will create a new one.

edges.condition: existing layout looks messy: score it before adding
edges.guidance: Flag problems: if the existing layout is messy (overlapping ops, orphaned ops outside annotations, broken grid alignment), tell the user before adding to it. Do not silently work around a bad layout.

edges.condition: any dock moved
edges.guidance: Verify (mandatory gate): after placing, re-check the layout. No turn that creates or moves operators may end without this check, and it must run during iterative building too -- not just at the very end.

edges.condition: another host with docked companions remains
edges.guidance: After you create ANY op with docked ops, you MUST place EVERY one of its docked ops directly below the host; if directly-below is occupied, place it directly to the host's right. Never leave a docked op where TD dropped it.

edges.condition: any placement happened
edges.guidance: Verify (mandatory gate): after placing, re-check the layout. No turn that creates or moves operators may end without this check, and it must run during iterative building too -- not just at the very end.
edges.pitfalls: Moving an operator without verifying the target coordinates are clear -- TD does not check for overlap when repositioning.

edges.condition: all batched positions applied; every new op placed
edges.guidance: Place, connect, then update the annotation to enclose the new operators, expanding its width/height as needed. If ops from the batch remain unplaced, stay in Set_Position and place the next one before taking this transition.

edges.condition: all batched positions applied; every op placed and no wiring is needed
edges.guidance: Place, connect, then update the annotation to enclose the new operators, expanding its width/height as needed. If ops from the batch remain unplaced, stay in Set_Position and place the next one before taking this transition.
edges.pitfalls: Creating operators without updating the enclosing annotation.

edges.condition: a moved op has docked companions
edges.guidance: After you create ANY op with docked ops, you MUST place EVERY one of its docked ops directly below the host; if directly-below is occupied, place it directly to the host's right. Never leave a docked op where TD dropped it.
edges.pitfalls: Leaving docked callback/info DATs at their auto-spawn position. TD drops them at arbitrary coordinates whenever they're created, whether by hand or by script.

edges.condition: always
edges.guidance: Read first: inspect the parent COMP's current layout and annotations in the network editor. Understand existing positions, groups, and flow before touching anything.

edges.condition: any annotation changed
edges.guidance: Verify (mandatory gate): after placing, re-check the layout. No turn that creates or moves operators may end without this check, and it must run during iterative building too -- not just at the very end.

edges.condition: another group remains to be laid out
edges.guidance: Identify the target group: Determine which annotation group the new operator belongs to. If none fits, you will create a new one.

edges.condition: zero violations
edges.guidance: Verify (mandatory gate): confirm no overlaps, nothing left at (0, 0), every docked op hugs its host, every wire flows forward, no ops outside annotations, grid alignment intact.

edges.condition: dock-hug violation reported
edges.guidance: ABSOLUTE RULE -- every docked op hugs its host, every time, no exceptions. If a slot collides with any other op (dock or not), move that other op to a clear region and recompute -- never thread docks around obstacles, never overlap, never leave one stranded.
edges.pitfalls: Leaving docked callback/info DATs at their auto-spawn position. TD drops them at arbitrary coordinates whenever they're created, whether by hand or by script.

edges.condition: overlap, origin, or forward-flow violation reported
edges.guidance: Confirm: no overlaps (use actual nodeWidth -- COMPs are wider than TOPs); nothing left at (0, 0); every wire flows forward (each source's nodeX + nodeWidth is left of its destination's nodeX -- no backward S wire).
edges.pitfalls: Using fixed offsets like nodeX + 300 without accounting for nodeWidth -- this is the #1 cause of overlapping operators when ops are wider than ~100 units.
